detail.readme:
# AutoShade ### Describe the picture. Keep the RAW. AI decides *what* to change — a deterministic Rust engine *does* it.
An editable, Lightroom-ready recipe instead of AI pixels.
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-v1.18.5-146b5a?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/skymanbp/autoshade/releases/tag/v1.18.5) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows%20·%20macOS%20·%20Linux-0b4b3f?style=flat-square)](#install-and-quickstart) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-1.94-a34b29?style=flat-square&logo=rust&logoColor=white)](rust-toolchain.toml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-4f5e5a?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **[Download v1.18.5](https://github.com/skymanbp/autoshade/releases/tag/v1.18.5)**  ·  [Website](https://autoshade.dev/)  ·  [Manual](docs/USER_MANUAL.md)  ·  [Showcase](docs/SHOWCASE.md)  ·  [In depth](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md)
Straight conversion → generated target → recovered recipe on the 61 MP RAW → same recipe after AI denoise. Bottom row: 1:1 crops.

> [!TIP] > **The generated picture is a target, never the delivery.** An image model paints the look you describe; > AutoShade fits an editable develop recipe to it and renders that recipe on the full-resolution RAW. > The recipe carries the look, the sensor carries the detail — and in the recipe path, **the AI never touches a pixel.** **Two AI paths, kept apart in the app, the command line and this page:** - **AI generation & reverse-fit** — an image model paints the picture you describe from your own frame (`reimagine`), and the reverse fit recovers that look as an editable recipe on the full RAW (`match`); one five-step strength control, Light to Full + AI review, sets how far the fit may go. The generated pixels are only ever a target. - **AI analysis & auto develop** — a vision model looks at the photo and proposes the recipe directly (`analyze`, `auto`), guided by your reference library or a typed direction; when its own visual review finds that develop clearly improvable, the model states how the finished picture should measure instead, the reverse fit finds the recipe, and the review picks between the two; **AI adjust** sends the develop you are looking at with a request ("darken the sky a little") and gets the complete adjusted recipe back, with any part it names selected by a content mask cut locally.
## Highlights
**🎯 Reverse-fit any look**
`reimagine` generates the picture from your frame; `match` recovers a recipe from it — or from any finished rendition of the same shot. Look error **0.161 → 0.023**. 		**🌌 A RAW denoiser trained here**
Cleans the sensor mosaic before demosaic. Keeps **98.70 %** of 17,817 faint stars on a real ISO 2500 frame.
**📐 Every slider is a written law**
Tone, Texture, Sharpening, masks and lens geometry are closed-form laws with named constants, each pinned by its own test. 		**🔁 Round-trips through Lightroom**
An exported .xmp is merged byte for byte into Lightroom's own; the full develop survives a Lightroom rewrite and imports back exactly.
**🖼️ Your library is the style guide**
Point it at finished photos you love; each develop sees the 3 closest as a reference. Embeddings run locally. 		**🧩 Local AI masks, no API key**
Subject, sky and point-prompted objects (BiRefNet, OneFormer, SAM 2.1), plus HDR, focus and noise stacking.
## Showcase Reverse-fit. Prompt: “a clearer afternoon, a little more contrast, a slightly deeper blue sky.” The recipe renders the look on the 9504 × 6336 RAW; the generated frame carries neither the detail nor the resolution.
One RAW, four looks. Straight conversion, then moody, golden and vivid — only the direction text changes.
ISO 2500 star field, 1:1. AutoShade with no denoise, then its own denoiser at 71 %. Clean colour, natural grain, faint stars intact.

Every number and prompt → Showcase

## What is new here Six techniques you will not find in another RAW developer. Each is written up in full — equations, figures, refused training runs — in **[AutoShade in depth](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md)**. | | Technique | In one line | |:-:|---|---| | **1** | [Generate, then reverse-fit](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#1-whole-image-ai-generation-then-reverse-fit-an-editable-recipe-from-any-finished-look) | An editable recipe from any finished look, solved at the distribution level | | **2** | [Evidence-gated local fit](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#2-how-the-reverse-fit-decides-divergence-evidence-gates-and-a-priced-local-field) | A divergence score `D` picks full solve or bounded mode; every local move must earn its place | | **3** | [Style by retrieval](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#3-style-reference-is-retrieval-over-your-whole-catalogue-not-a-preset) | SigLIP 2 search over your own finished photos, not a preset | | **4** | [Every slider is a written law](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#4-every-develop-control-is-a-written-law-pinned-by-the-projects-own-tests) | Tone, Texture, Sharpening, masks and lens geometry as closed-form laws, each pinned by its own test | | **5** | [A denoiser with pre-written pass marks](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#5-the-raw-denoiser-is-trained-here-and-judged-by-pass-marks-written-before-the-run) | Trained on this project's data; two later runs failed their marks and were refused | | **6** | [The camera's own look](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#6-the-cameras-own-look-is-read-from-the-picture-like-with-like) | A per-photo base curve read from the embedded preview, like with like | ## How it works - **One engine, three front ends** — desktop app, CLI and loopback web UI share one Rust library and one per-user develop store. - **Local first** — eight Python sidecars (masks, two denoisers, correspondence, descriptions, embeddings, depth for the lens blur, faces) run on your machine; pixels leave it only for an AI operation you ask for. The desktop app asks GitHub at most once a day whether a newer version is out — that request carries the program's name and version and nothing of yours, and it can be turned off (Settings → About). - **Non-destructive** — your photo library stays read-only; generated pixels always land on their own labelled card. Diagram generated from [autoshade.architecture.json](docs/architecture/autoshade.architecture.json) · [zoom it online](https://autoshade.dev/architecture.html) · full design in [ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) ## Measured numbers | What | Measured | |---|---| | Automated test battery | 2077 library / 30 CLI / 383 GUI / 2+2 contract tests | | RAW coverage | 24 extensions · 725 camera bodies · nine-camera zoo 9/9 | | Reverse-fit, stone viaduct | look error 0.161 → 0.023 at confidence 0.63 | | Reverse-fit, desert canyon | look error 0.129 → 0.048 · sky ΔE 3.8 | | Faint stars kept through the denoiser | 98.70 % of 17,817 stars on an ISO 2500 frame | The full table — 20+ rows with conditions and sources — is in [AutoShade in depth](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#measured-numbers); [`scripts/check_docs.py`](scripts/check_docs.py) re-derives the pinned claims. ## Install and quickstart | Platform | Get it | |---|---| | **Windows** | `AutoShade-Setup-1.18.5.exe` — per-user, no admin. Or the portable `autoshade-1.18.5-windows-x64.zip` | | **macOS** | `AutoShade-1.18.5-macos-universal.zip` (Apple silicon + Intel), or `-macos-cli.zip` | | **Linux** | `AutoShade-1.18.5-linux-x64.zip` — command line only | All on the **[v1.18.5 release page](https://github.com/skymanbp/autoshade/releases/tag/v1.18.5)**. Python 3 is needed only for the local AI sidecars; model weights download on first use. > [!NOTE] > **macOS:** the app is ad-hoc signed, not notarised — on first launch use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** (once per machine). **Desktop app** — it starts on a mode page (Landscape, Portraits, Normal; see [Choosing a mode](docs/USER_MANUAL.md#choosing-a-mode)); then open a photo (`Ctrl+O`), move a slider, export with `Ctrl+Shift+E`. The original is never touched. **Normal** is a short one-click panel for phone and jpg photos ([Normal mode](docs/USER_MANUAL.md#normal-mode)). **CLI** ```bash # manual develop autoshade apply photo.ARW recipe.json -o developed.tif # AI develop, end to end autoshade auto photo.ARW --guidance "natural color; protect highlights" -o developed.tif # describe a look, then recover it as an editable recipe on the RAW autoshade reimagine photo.ARW --prompt "a clearer afternoon, deeper blue sky" autoshade match photo.ARW out/photo.reimagine.png --render ``` Upgrades, silent installs and every command: **[User manual](docs/USER_MANUAL.md)**.
Release assets and checksums
Built by GitHub Actions from the tag; `checksums.txt` carries every SHA-256. The RAW denoiser weights are uploaded by hand to the release the sidecar pins — [`releases/download/v1.6.0/autoshade-raw-denoise-v2.pth`](https://github.com/skymanbp/autoshade/releases/download/v1.6.0/autoshade-raw-denoise-v2.pth), mirrored byte-exact on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Azng0/autoshade-mirror-autoshade-raw-denoise) — and refused unless size and SHA-256 match the pin in `python/denoise_raw.py`. | File | Size | SHA-256 | |---|---:|---| | `autoshade.exe` (CLI) | 26,305,024 bytes | `02b8c5b59140568b7c181fd74d39734a921f777ec8bebaaa3b93821c170adf9e` | | `autoshade-gui.exe` (desktop app) | 33,923,072 bytes | `3ffcc73d93ca987fd829d001430fe67aa01a6fbb6bd400a9e5b65249656d8068` | | `AutoShade-Setup-1.18.5.exe` (installer) | 17,001,002 bytes | `b133f5b03f2b5e3581d2fb8af33a1d3ed42a1b07de594ef006853e5d0de5fff0` | | `autoshade-1.18.5-windows-x64.zip` (portable archive) | 23,123,635 bytes | `90501b97a9ea819ebdedd207ed4774599f0ecd7abc3db331810a744e3027e9e9` | | `AutoShade-1.18.5-macos-universal.zip` (macOS app bundle) | 46,321,055 bytes | `70db2d469e6751ac9f0b4bef4569b76d79b76a101a085ac535f01379fdf3374a` | | `AutoShade-1.18.5-linux-x64.zip` (Linux command line only) | 11,092,943 bytes | `5ca35b82ae55a284056e03596cdf70ec149bfc90449d2f566e12d1b0f664494f` | | `AutoShade-1.18.5-macos-cli.zip` (macOS command line only) | 20,137,259 bytes | `a1b158500cf51812dc87ba120b228a89a8814cc75e70ffaa1a50eb822eba0a12` | | `autoshade-raw-denoise-v2.pth` (RAW denoiser weights, fetched on demand from the v1.6.0 release) | 130,590,559 bytes | `ffafa40a53f52092149db2fcf03636117ad6855e1068142d4f6b03b634e9f9c4` |
Build from source
Rust edition 2024, rustc/cargo 1.94. ```bash cargo build --release # CLI cargo build --release --features gui --bin autoshade-gui # desktop app ``` Local AI tools need Python packages (weights download on first use): | Tool | Packages | |---|---| | Subject mask (BiRefNet) | `torchvision timm einops` | | Subject fallback (U²-Net) | `rembg` | | Sky / objects (OneFormer, SAM 2.1) | `transformers torch` | | AI denoise | `torch opencv-python numpy einops requests` |
## Supported formats

.cr2 · Canon EOS 40D
.cr3 · Canon EOS R6
.nef · Nikon D700

.arw · Sony α7 III
.orf · Olympus E-M5
.rw2 · Panasonic DMC-GX85

.pef · Pentax K-5
.dng · Ricoh GR II
.raf · Fujifilm X-S10 — X-Trans, approximate
Nine real CC0 files, fully decoded and neutral-rendered — not embedded previews.
**Camera RAW — 24 extensions** ```text arw, dng, raw, raf, nef, cr2, cr3, orf, rw2, pef, srw, 3fr, fff, iiq, mef, mos, erf, kdc, dcr, dcs, crw, nrw, mrw, ari ``` Decoded by rawler 0.7.2, which carries **725 camera models**. **No embedded preview:** 12 of the 24 formats store none. They are `orf`, `srw`, `nrw`, `mef`, `mos`, `kdc`, `dcr`, `dcs`, `erf`, `iiq`, `crw`, and `ari`; AutoShade renders its own neutral version instead. **Baked rasters — 8 extensions:** `jpg` `jpeg` `png` `tif` `tiff` `bmp` `webp` `gif`, with ICC conversion. ## Tech stack **Rust** (rustc/cargo 1.94, edition 2024) · rawler · image · qcms · rayon · egui/eframe · tiny_http — **Python** sidecars on PyTorch. RAW decode, 24 formats, 725 bodies · deterministic f32 develop engine · hand-rolled XMP layer (no XML crate) for byte-exact Lightroom merges. The current battery is **2077 library (2054 pass + 23 `#[ignore]`d forensic probes) / 30 CLI / 383 GUI / 2+2 contract** tests. Per-subsystem notes: [In depth → Implementation](docs/DEEP_DIVE.md#implementation) · equations and provenance: [TECH_STACK.md](docs/TECH_STACK.md). ## Status and limitations - **Release gates at v1.18.5** cover the CLI, desktop GUI, sidecar contracts, format fixtures and the deterministic renderer. - **Not in scope:** Adobe's rendering (AutoShade is its own develop engine; a sidecar carries the same settings to Lightroom, which renders them its own way), an exact X-Trans demosaic, a notarised macOS build, a Linux desktop app. - **Honest markers:** AI masks are local re-creations, not Adobe's pixels; the macOS app is CI-verified but has no reported interactive users yet. - Release ledger and rulings: [ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). ## License **MIT** — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Showcase photographs © 2026 skymanbp, all rights reserved (not MIT).
Models, fonts and samples
Model weights download separately and remain their authors' property; every pinned model also has a byte-exact mirror on Hugging Face (`Azng0/autoshade-mirror-*`), checksum-verified either way — table in [`python/_mirror.py`](python/_mirror.py). | Model | Purpose | License | |---|---|---| | SCUNet | AI denoise (baked sources) | Apache-2.0 | | DRUNet-colour (DPIR), fine-tuned here as `autoshade-raw-denoise-v2.pth` | AI denoise (RAW mosaic) | MIT; fine-tuning pairs from RawNIND, CC BY-SA 4.0 | | BiRefNet | Subject segmentation | MIT | | U²-Net | Subject fallback | Apache-2.0 | | OneFormer ADE20K | Sky segmentation | MIT | | SAM 2.1 | Point-prompted object masks | Apache-2.0 | | MoGe-2 ViT-L (code in `python/_moge/`) | AI lens blur depth map | MIT (DINOv2 backbone code Apache-2.0) | | MediaPipe Face Landmarker (BlazeFace + Face Mesh V2) | Portraits mode face and eye outlines | Apache-2.0 | | SigLIP 2 | Style embeddings | Apache-2.0 | | Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct | Local look descriptions | Apache-2.0 | | Stable Diffusion 2.1 | DIFT correspondence field | CreativeML Open RAIL++-M | **Fonts:** subset Noto faces (SIL OFL) and a Lucide icon face (ISC) — texts in `assets/fonts/`. **RAW samples:** the nine format-grid files are from [raw.pixls.us](https://raw.pixls.us/) under CC0 1.0, SHA-256-verified. Thanks to the rawler, image, qcms, rayon, clap, serde, ureq, egui/eframe, tiny_http and local-model communities.

Made for photographers who want to know what the AI changed — in numbers.
